# Psalm 42 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 42:1 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** For-the-choirmaster. A-Maskil of-the-sons of-Korah.
- **LOGOS:** For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the Sons of Korah.
- **PNEUMA:** For the music director. A psalm of the descendants of Korah.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 42:8 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Deep calls to-deep at-the-sound of-Your-waterfalls; all Your-breakers and-Your-waves have-gone over-me.
- **LOGOS:** Deep calls to deep at the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and Your waves have gone over me.
- **PNEUMA:** I hear the tumult of the raging seas as Your waves and surging tides sweep over me.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 42:9 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** By-day YHWH commands His-steadfast-love, and-by-night His-song [is] with-me — a-prayer to-the-God of-my-life.
- **LOGOS:** By day the LORD commands His steadfast love, and at night His song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
- **PNEUMA:** But each day the LORD pours His unfailing love upon me, and through each night I sing His songs, praying to God who gives me life.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 42:5 (overlap: 3%)

- **EMET:** These I-remember, and-I-pour-out upon-me my-soul: how I-went with-the-throng; I-led-them to-the-house of-God with-the-voice of-a-shout-of-joy and-thanksgiving, a-multitude keeping-festival.
- **LOGOS:** These things I remember, as I pour out my soul: how I would go with the throng and lead them in procession to the house of God with glad shouts and songs of praise, a multitude keeping festival.
- **PNEUMA:** My heart is breaking as I remember how it used to be: I walked among the crowds of worshipers, leading a great procession to the house of God, singing for joy and giving thanks amid the sound of a great celebration!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 42:7 (overlap: 5%)

- **EMET:** My-God, upon-me my-soul is-cast-down; therefore I-remember-You from-the-land of-the-Jordan and-the-Hermons, from-Mount Mizar.
- **LOGOS:** My soul is cast down within me; therefore I remember You from the land of Jordan and of Hermon, from Mount Mizar.
- **PNEUMA:** Now I am deeply discouraged, but I will remember You — even from distant Mount Hermon, the source of the Jordan, from the land of Mount Mizar.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 42:10 (overlap: 5%)

- **EMET:** I-say to-God, my-Rock, 'Why have-You-forgotten-me? Why do-I-go mourning because-of the-oppression of-the-enemy?'
- **LOGOS:** I say to God, my rock: 'Why have You forgotten me? Why do I go mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?'
- **PNEUMA:** 'O God my rock,' I cry, 'why have You forgotten me? Why must I wander around in grief, oppressed by my enemies?'

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
